item.description: Game-changing global nature pact still has potential – but nations need to speed up progress, conservationists urge.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 12th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 12th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: You could own an entire Scottish island for €414,000 – but there’s a catch
item.description: Hildasay Island off the west coast of Shetland offers spectacular views and birdlife, but no real creature comforts.

item.title: ‘We still love you’: NATO envoy seeks to reassure Europe over US military pullback
item.description: US Ambassador to NATO, Matthew Whitaker, has enthused that there is no “love” lost between Washington and Brussels amid a more Europeanised NATO.

item.title: Zelenskyy says Russia ignored Trump's 'energy ceasefire' and kept attacking Ukraine
item.description: Zelenskyy addressed the Warsaw Security Forum in one of his first reactions to renewed turmoil with Washington, following Trump's surprise energy ceasefire announcement and controversial diesel deal with Russia.

item.title: IEA urges additional diesel releases ahead of key meeting
item.description: Tightening global diesel markets prompted the International Energy Agency to call on its members to accelerate previously agreed releases from strategic oil reserves, prioritising diesel. The IEA also asked member states to assess "whether additional diesel releases are necessary".

item.title: Chinese carmaker BYD considers opening a factory in France
item.description: France is among the European countries where BYD is considering opening a plant. According to vice-president Stella Li, "France is on the shortlist".

item.title: Independent Gibala beats Tusk’s party to win Krakow mayoral run-off
item.description: The new mayor took 62% of the vote in an election triggered after residents voted in May to oust his predecessor, and Łukasz Gibała warned that the city’s finances are in a disastrous state.

item.title: Cute cats and street fighters: The best things to do, hear, see or watch in Europe this week
item.description: Fontaines D.C. bring synths and psychedelia with their latest album 'Dopamine Chamber' while a new exhibition near Paris explores all things cute. Here's what to look out for this week.

item.title: EU leaders face budget showdown as Germany leads revolt over spending plans
item.description: An Irish compromise proposal for the EU’s long-term budget has drawn fire from the net-paying countries over its size and its focus on cutting ‘modern’ priorities. The Commission and MEPs have countered, warning of the risks of a less ambitious, more rigid budget.

item.title: What is ‘pilgra-merch’? The travel trend turning souvenirs into trip inspiration
item.description: Tourists are showing off how well-travelled they are through destination-specific grocery tote bags or branded hotel caps.

item.title: Fire totally destroys oldest covered food market in Paris, authorities say
item.description: The Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges in the Marais district has existed since 1615 and draws its name from the red outfits that orphans wore at a hospital near the market until 1772.

item.title: EU decries 'concerning' Trump-Putin deal, insists sanctions on Russia will continue
item.description: The Trump-Putin diesel deal has been badly received by EU foreign ministers, who say it undermines transatlantic unity at a time when Russia intensifies its attacks on Ukraine.

item.title: Footage shows Glucksmann covered in flour after winning French left-wing presidential primary
item.description: French politician and European Parliament member Raphaël Glucksmann was pelted with flour outside a bar in Paris on Sunday evening, shortly after winning the social-democratic left’s primary for the 2027 presidential election with more than 66% of the vote.

item.title: CCTV shows moment of strike at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh
item.description: CTV footage released by Saudi authorities shows the moment a missile strike hit Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on October 10. The attack killed at least 13 people and injured hundreds, forcing the suspension of airport operations.

item.title: Judge orders Trump to pull taxpayer-funded adverts
item.description: The White House calls the adverts, reportedly paid for with $20 million of Homeland Security funds, public service announcements, but they have drawn criticism from both parties.

item.title: France’s main problem is its inability to reduce public debt, economist says
item.description: French economist Nicolas Bouzou says France's economic growth is not "strong" enough to sustain the country's welfare state.

item.title: Tens of thousands march in Brussels demanding urgent climate action
item.description: Tens of thousands of people marched through Brussels on Sunday, 11 October, demanding stronger action on climate change ahead of next month's COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey.

item.title: Spain national day military parade: 4,380 troops, 82 aircraft and Dragón armoured vehicles debut
item.description: Madrid puts on its finery for the National Day of Spain parade, with general elections looming and tensions high over the housing crisis and migration pressures.

item.title: Opposition figures and journalists allege police abuses during India protests
item.description: The protests were triggered by allegations of manipulating voter lists during a nationwide roll revision that critics say could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.

item.title: 'NATO's KPI is peace', Latvia's foreign minister says
item.description: Baiba Braže, Latvia's foreign minister, believes NATO's eastern flank is well protected at a time when it is facing heightened tensions. Latvia and its Baltic neighbours are once again on alert amid growing concerns over Russian drones and airspace violations.

item.title: Mystery of La Navidad: site of first Spanish settlement in Americas unknown
item.description: On Christmas Eve 1492 the Santa María ran aground off Haiti; Columbus used its timbers to build Fort Navidad, where 39 men died. More than five centuries later, archaeologists have yet to pinpoint the site.

item.title: Why does the EU want a European Security Council? Take our poll
item.description: The EU wants to build a new security mechanism to face hybrid threats, like drone incursions, cyberattacks and sabotage. But does it really need a new Security Council?

item.title: How can a new Security Council boost the EU's defence strategy? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot
item.description: The EU is reviving the idea of a European Security Council as Russia's hybrid attacks continue and reliance on US commitment to NATO remains risky. But how could this look like? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot.

item.title: Rare Kandinsky masterpiece and Hockney’s beloved dog painting head to London auction
item.description: Around 50 works by some of the biggest names in modern and contemporary art are going under the hammer at Christie’s in London on Wednesday 14 October.

item.title: Trump turns the screws on Kyiv as EU budget talks hit a wall
item.description: Good morning. It’s Monday. I’m Mared Gwyn. Today: Europe braces as Trump turns up the heat on Zelenskyy, and Ireland’s EU budget compromise falls dead on arrival.

item.title: UK’s Burnham says Russia interfered in Brexit vote
item.description: The prime minister said Germany’s Friedrich Merz had told him the far-right AfD was linked to Russia, as he faces questions at home over Labour’s ties to the UAE.

item.title: Addictive behaviour is falling among Portuguese teens but most vulnerable are still exposed
item.description: Portuguese teenagers are drinking and using drugs less and facing fewer problems, but risks are increasingly concentrated among those with multiple vulnerabilities, according to a new ICAD study on addictive behaviours.

item.title: Europe Today: Trump claims Ukraine-Russia energy ceasefire as Baltics stay on alert
item.description: Donald Trump says Russia and Ukraine have agreed an energy ceasefire. Volodymyr Zelenskyy says it was news to him. As he addresses the Warsaw Security Forum, we hear from Latvia's FM Baiba Braže, Doha after a deadly Riyadh airport attack, and France's debt fears.

item.title: North Korea fires 'several ballistic missiles' into Sea of Japan, Seoul's military says
item.description: South Korea's National Security Office convened an emergency security meeting following the launch to review the country's military readiness.

item.title: IKEA has just launched another second-hand marketplace. But will it stop producing ‘fast furniture’?
item.description: Sustainability is noticeably absent in IKEA’s latest press statement about its second-hand marketplace.

item.title: Rockies, Route 66 and railway hotels: Why 2027 is the year to explore the US by train
item.description: The United States is marking 200 years of passenger rail travel with scenic long-distance routes, vintage steam trains, historic stations and unusual railway stays. Here’s how to explore the country by train in 2027.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 12th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 12th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Which European countries are hit the hardest by annual rent inflation and why?
item.description: Rent prices have risen significantly across Europe, and in particular in Romania and Croatia in recent periods. Euronews Business takes a closer look at annual rent inflation with a focus on these two countries.

item.title: Lumière festival 2026 in Lyon: Stars share their first cinema memories
item.description: For its 18th edition, the Lumière Festival opened in Lyon to a full house. Over nine days and nights, the French city will present around 450 screenings in honour of classic cinema and the brother's Ethan and Joel Coen.

item.title: Oil prices drop as stocks rise after Trump touts 'energy ceasefire'
item.description: Most stock markets rose early Monday as oil prices fell after Donald Trump announced an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine, which offset a fresh wave of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

item.title: 'Energy ceasefire': Confusion in Kyiv, support from allies, silence from Moscow and fresh strikes
item.description: Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, but Moscow has not confirmed it. Zelenskyy expressed surprise and reported fresh Russian strikes on Ukrainian power plants, causing outages.

item.title: Judo: Japan reclaim mixed team world title with eighth gold in Baku
item.description: Japan reclaimed the Mixed Team World Championship title in Baku, defeating Russia in the final to secure their eighth gold. After overcoming China in the semi-final, Japan sealed victory through Akari Omori, while Russia reached their first-ever mixed team final.

item.title: Shakira sets Amazon Music record in Madrid with most-watched live stream by a female artist
item.description: The global broadcast of the Colombian singer's Madrid concert has become the most-watched live performance by a female artist on Amazon Music. The platform highlights the role of the Spanish capital as a bridge between Latin America and Europe.

item.title: Antarctic penguins emit up to 7 million tonnes of methane a year, study finds
item.description: A study by CSIC and the University of Granada finds that chinstrap penguin colonies are a previously unmeasured natural source of methane, emitting up to 7 million tonnes a year.

item.title: French Social democratic primary: Raphaël Glucksmann wins big in first round
item.description: With more than 66% in the primary, French MEP Raphaël Glucksmann is chosen as the social-democratic candidate for France’s 2027 presidential election. On X, he insists that "a left true to its values can unite, govern and win".

item.title: Nepal orders evacuations after landslide triggers Budhi Gandaki flash flood
item.description: Nepal’s authorities ordered residents along the Budhi Gandaki River to evacuate on Sunday, 11 October, after a sudden flash flood swept away homes and other buildings in the country’s mountainous north-central region.

item.title: Tens of thousands urge EU for climate action at Brussels demonstration
item.description: Ahead of a major UN summit, thousands of protesters marched through the streets of Brussels demanding greater action to combat climate change.

item.title: Police clear Guano beach camp in Ceuta days before royal visit
item.description: Spain's National Police have cleared Guano beach in Ceuta, where about 400 migrants were still camped, two days before the King and Queen visit the city. It was the last remaining camp; some migrants fled to the nearby hills.

item.title: Paris motor show: Macron calls for European preference against China
item.description: On Monday, the French president will open his final Paris Motor Show, pushing his "Made in Europe" agenda: tying state aid for this key industry to genuinely EU-based production.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 11th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 11th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Nepal flash floods sweep away houses, five people missing
item.description: Rescuers have been battling to rescue people affected by the flash floods in Nepal that swept 45 houses and left five people missing.

item.title: Russia strikes power plants in Ukraine despite 'energy ceasefire' announced by Trump
item.description: After Donald Trump's criticism blaming Volodymyr Zelenskyy for high diesel prices, suggesting Ukraine should get a new leader, US President announced Russia and Ukraine had agreed on an 'energy ceasefire', but Russia struck Ukrainian power plants hours after the announcement.

item.title: Hochvogel mountain at risk of major collapse as 400,000 cubic metres of rock threatens to break away
item.description: The Hochvogel sits on the border between Germany and the Austrian region of Tyrol. It is part of the Allgäu High Alps and stands at 2,592 metres high.

item.title: 'Up to our people' to pick leader, Zelenskyy responds to Trump's pledge for new elections in Ukraine
item.description: Only Russia is responsible for the war in Ukraine, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday in a TV interview, responding to criticism from US President Donald Trump, who blamed him for high diesel prices and said he should be replaced.
